# Introduction to `ggplot()` {data-stack-name="ggplot()"}

## ggplot layers

- ggplot is a package for making plots
- ggplot uses layers. Each layer is added with the `+` symbol
    - Layer1 + Layer2 + Layer3
    - Every layer adds something new to the plot

##

::::: columns
:::: column

#### Layer 1: basic info
::: nonincremental
1. Specify the data table
2. Specify the x and y variables in `aes()`
:::
```r
ggplot(table_name, aes(x=column1, y=column2))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

table_name <- tibble(column1=rnorm(10,2,n=100), column2 = column1*2 + rnorm(0,1,n=100))
ggplot(table_name, aes(x=column1, y=column2))
```
::::

:::: column
#### Layer 2: actual plot

::: nonincremental
- geom_histogram() adds histogram layer
- geom_point() adds scatter plot layer
:::
```r
# Histogram
ggplot(...) + geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(table_name, aes(x=column1)) + geom_histogram()
```

```r
# Scatter plot
ggplot(...) + geom_point()

```

```{r}
ggplot(table_name, aes(x=column1, y=column2)) + geom_point()
```
::::
:::::

## Part 1 output

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(3)

mean_height = 65
x = 25:105
sample_size = 25
n_samples = 4

density <- round(dnorm(x=x, mean= 65, sd=2)*n_samples*sample_size)

Heights <- numeric(0)

for (i in 1:length(x)){
Heights <- c(Heights, rep(x[i], times = density[i]))
}

RandomSample <- numeric(0)
for (i in 1:n_samples){
    RandomSample <- c(RandomSample, rep(paste0("RandomSample", i), times = sample_size))
}

sample_heights <- tibble(Heights=sample(Heights), RandomSample = RandomSample)

#write_csv(sample_heights, "data/sample_heights.csv")

head(sample_heights)

```

## Part 2 plots


:::: columns
::: column

```{r}
ggplot(sample_heights, aes(x=Heights)) + geom_histogram()
```

:::
::: column

```{r}
ggplot(sample_heights, aes(x=Heights)) + geom_histogram() + facet_wrap(~RandomSample)
```
:::
::::

## Part 3 plots
:::: columns
::: column
```{r}

sample_heights <- sample_heights %>% mutate(ShiftedHeights = Heights - 65)

ggplot(sample_heights, aes(x=ShiftedHeights)) + geom_histogram()

```
:::
::: column

```{r}

sample_heights <- sample_heights %>% mutate(TransformedHeights = ShiftedHeights/2)

ggplot(sample_heights, aes(x=TransformedHeights)) + geom_histogram()

```
:::
